_note: The heart events (data/events/heart_<villager>.json): one short scene per villager when their heart band first reaches 3 and the farmer talks to them. One part per villager, started at its id. Our own scenes.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Ah, it's you. Sit with me a minute? My knees and I have been arguing all morning.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: You know, I kept a little packet back every year. Eggplant seed, from the plants by my door.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: My hands are too slow for a whole row now. But a farmer who stops to talk to an old woman... you'd look after them.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: I'll give them the best corner of the field.

lines.speaker: tome
lines.text: Bring me the first one that ripens. That's all the thanks I want.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Hey... can you keep a secret? A real one, not a baby one.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: There's a big carp in the pond. Old and black, with one white spot. I've seen it three times and nobody believes me.

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: If you catch it, don't sell it. Just look at it and let it go. Promise?

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Pinky swear counts double. You're alright, you know that?

lines.speaker: kota
lines.text: Fine! Then I'll catch it first, and I won't even show you. ...Maybe I'll show you.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Oh, good. Could you hold this end of the ledger? The wind keeps turning the pages.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: My father kept this store for thirty years. Some days I think I'm only minding it until someone better comes.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: Then a farmer walks in every week asking for seeds, and the shelves have to be full, and I forget to worry.

lines.speaker: sayo
lines.text: So, thank you. For being a reason. I'll stop talking before I embarrass us both.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Wait. Let me see your hands.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Calluses in the right places now. When you came, you held a hoe like a broom.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: My teacher said a tool remembers who uses it well. I never believed him until I was old.

lines.speaker: hachiro
lines.text: Bring yours by whenever the edge goes. I'll look at them first. That's not for everyone.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Oh, good timing! Hold still and open your mouth. ...I mean, please try this.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: My mother's sweet bean paste. I've made it every week for six years, and it has never once tasted like hers.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Everyone here says it's lovely. They're being kind. You came from outside, so tell me true.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Hm. As polite as the rest of them. I'll take it anyway, and keep trying.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Too sweet... She used less sugar in the lean years, and never went back. Of course! Why didn't I see it?

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Come by again. The second cup is on the house for you. Only for you. Don't tell Ichiro.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...You. Come here. Listen.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: Hear that? Good charcoal rings when you knock two pieces together. Bad charcoal just thuds.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: My father's rang every time. Mine still thuds, mostly. Thirty years at it.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: You work the soil the same way. Every day, nobody watching. ...Here. One for your stove.

lines.speaker: farmer
lines.text: Listen. This one rings.

lines.speaker: ichiro
lines.text: ...Hm. So it does. Don't tell anyone. They'll all want one.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Come here. Cup your hands.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Well water. I told you it's cold all year. Now taste it, properly. Slowly.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: My wife tasted the well every morning. Sweet meant the thaw was near. Iron meant a dry month. She was right more often than the radio. So. What does it say to you?

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Iron and sweet... a dry month, then. I thought so. She'd have smiled at that.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Ha. Honest. It takes years to taste the rest. Keep drinking.

lines.speaker: genzo
lines.text: Here. Seed rice from my last good sack. Sow it where the water stays. Don't tell Haru, she'll want some.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: There you are! Stand still. No, on the mat. Both feet. I need to see how wide you walk.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Grandma taught me on sandals. The first pair I ever made was hers, all lumps. She wore them every day until the soles came apart.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: So now everyone I like gets a pair. That's the rule. Tight weave or loose? Tight lasts, loose is kind to your feet.

choices.text: Tight. The field is hard on them.
Loose. Be kind to my feet.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: A working pair, then. I'll twist a little rice straw from Genzo's racks into the heel. He won't miss it.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: Ha! That's what Grandma always said. Soft feet make a soft temper. Loose it is.

lines.speaker: haru
lines.text: They'll be ready by the end of the week. And here, cucumber seed I saved from my best vines. Grow me something to brag about.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Ah, good timing. Hold this pole straight for me. ...There. Nana's scarecrow. Old hoe handles and my second-best hat.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: She says it's me. The crows took every tomato last summer, and she says only I scowl hard enough to scare them off.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: She left the face for me to finish. She painted a frown, as a hint. What do you think? A second opinion settles arguments in this house.

choices.text: Keep the frown for the crows.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: A smile... My wife used to say I glared at seedlings as if they owed me money. All right. One smiling Shige, at least.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Ha! Nana will be furious that I agreed with her. The crows, too. Frown it is.

lines.speaker: shige
lines.text: Here, for the help. Tomato seed from the few plants the crows left alone. Clever plants. Grow them where you can keep an eye on them.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Hey, farmer! Quick: where are the fish right now? The fast water by the rocks, or the dark pool under the bank?

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Ha! Most people pick the pool. In summer they sit in the fast water, where the air is. You've got river eyes.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: That's what everyone picks. In winter you'd be right. Today they're up in the riffle, gulping air. Lesson one.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Father poled the ferry here thirty years and never caught more than me. Here, a daikon from behind the hut. Simmer it with a river fish. Nothing else needed.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: You came at the right time. Sit on the step. I'm going to tell you about the shrine's fox.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Grandfather said a white fox walks the gravel on misty nights, checking that every lantern is lit. He'd leave it a rice ball.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: The rice ball was always gone by morning. ...Do you believe in the fox?

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Maybe a little! That's the right answer. That's exactly how much Grandfather believed.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Ha! Only in daylight. Then come by at dusk sometime, and we'll see how brave you are.

lines.speaker: kaede
lines.text: Here, turnip seed from the offering box. The fox doesn't eat turnips. I checked.
